;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[October 2020 Afghanistan attacks]]
***A bomb kills at least five people and injures another nine in [[Grishk District]], [[Helmand Province]]. [https://tolonews.com/afghanistan-166936 (TOLOnews)]
***A bus hits a roadside bomb, killing two people and injuring another ten in [[Shindand District]], [[Herat Province]]. [https://tolonews.com/afghanistan-166936 (TOLOnews)]
*[[2020 Kyrgyzstan protests]]
**[[Kyrgyzstan]] special forces detain former [[President of Kyrgyzstan|President]] [[Almazbek Atambayev]] in a raid on his compound. Atambayev was freed from prison by anti-[[government of Kyrgyzstan|government]] protesters on October 5. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-54493185 (BBC News)]

;Arts and culture
* Luis Fonsi's [[Despacito]] music video becomes the first video on [[YouTube]] to surpass seven billion (7,000,000,000) views. [http://web.archive.org/web/20201010175649if_/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kJQP7kiw5Fk (Archive)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[2020 Atlantic hurricane season]]
**[[Hurricane Delta]]
***Delta weakens to a [[tropical storm]]. [https://news.sky.com/story/louisiana-downgraded-delta-continues-to-inflict-destruction-on-southern-us-communities-12100572 (Sky News)]
***Over 700,000 [[power outage]]s are reported in the [[U.S. state]]s of [[Louisiana]], [[Texas]], and [[Mississippi]]. [https://www.cbsnews.com/live-updates/hurricane-delta-tropical-storm-latest-news-updates-2020-10-10/ (CBS News)]
*[[2020 wildfire season]]
**Wildfires kill at least two people in [[Syria]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/10/10/at-least-two-killed-as-forest-fires-burn-in-syria-lebanon (Al Jazeera English)]

;Health and environment 
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Czech Republic]]
****The [[Government of the Czech Republic|government]] mull reimposing a lockdown as the [[Ministry of Health (Czech Republic)|health ministry]] reports 8,618 new cases on Friday, surpassing the previous record set on Thursday and reached a fourth straight daily record for the country where infection rate per capita (398 per 100,000) is the highest in the [[European Union]]. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/1746846/world (''Arab News'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]
****The number of confirmed cases in [[France]] increases by 26,896 to 718,873, setting a record for the largest number of reported cases since the beginning of the pandemic. [https://thehill.com/policy/international/520500-france-breaks-single-day-record-with-large-coronavirus-case-surge (''The Hill'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]]
****The number of confirmed cases in [[Germany]] increased by 4,721 to 319,381, according to data from the [[Robert Koch Institute]] for infectious diseases. It is the highest number of reported cases in a single day since April as the country tightens its restrictions in [[Berlin]] and [[Frankfurt]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/10/10/germany-tightens-covid-19-restrictions-as-numbers-surge-in-europe (Al Jazeera)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Republic of Ireland]]
****[[National Public Health Emergency Team]] reports 1,012 new cases in [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] in 24 hours. It is the highest number of reported cases in Ireland since April, when 1,068 cases were reported. [https://www.irishtimes.com/news/health/coronavirus-three-more-people-dead-and-1-012-new-cases-reported-as-hospital-numbers-near-200-1.4377770 (''The Irish Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal]]
****[[Portugal]] registers 1,646 new daily cases, bringing the cumulative total of confirmed cases to 85,574. This is the highest daily increase for the country since the beginning of the pandemic. [https://covid19.min-saude.pt/wp-content/uploads/2020/10/221_DGS_boletim_20201010.pdf (DGS)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine]]
****The number of daily deaths in [[Ukraine]] exceeds 100 for the first time since the pandemic began, jumping to 108, according to a statement from the [[National Security and Defense Council of Ukraine|NSDC]], with a total of 4,887 deaths being recorded since the first cases were reported in the country. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-ukraine-deaths/ukraine-reports-record-daily-jump-in-coronavirus-deaths-idUSKBN26V091 (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Russia]] reports 12,846 cases, their highest since the start of the pandemic. The number of cases reaches to 1,285,084. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-russia-cases/russia-reports-new-all-time-record-of-daily-coronavirus-cases-idUSKBN26V0BD (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in New York (state)]]
*****[[Governor of New York (state)|New York governor]] [[Andrew Cuomo]] announces that 826 people have been hospitalized with [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]], the highest number since July 15. [https://abcnews.go.com/Health/wireStory/religious-gathering-limit-upheld-ny-hospitalizations-rise-73540153 (ABC News)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Michigan]]
*****The [[Michigan Department of Health and Human Services]] reports that around 104,000 people in [[Michigan]] have recovered since the start of the pandemic. However, the state reported 1,522 new cases and 15 deaths, bringing the statewide total number of cases to 134,656 and death toll to 6,891. [https://www.mlive.com/coronavirus/2020/10/more-than-104000-michigan-residents-have-recovered-from-coronavirus-since-pandemic-began.html (Mlives.com)]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in the United States]]
*****[[Office of the Assistant Secretary for Preparedness and Response|Health and Human Services Assistant Secretary for Preparedness and Response]] [[Robert Kadlec]] says that the [[United States]] might expect deliveries of a [[COVID-19 vaccine]] in January 2021. [https://www.winknews.com/2020/10/10/trump-official-says-vaccine-expected-starting-in-january/ (Wink News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Manitoba]]
*****The [[Government of Manitoba|Manitoba government]] announced 97 new cases of COVID-19 in the province, setting a single-day record since the first cases reported in Manitoba. [https://winnipeg.ctvnews.ca/manitoba-sets-single-day-record-with-97-new-covid-19-cases-2-deaths-1.5140900 (CTV News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mexico]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Mexico]]
****[[Mexico]] announces that it will pay [[Mexican peso|$]]159.88 million to the [[World Health Organization]] to secure vaccine access through the agency’s [[COVID-19 vaccine|COVAX]] plan. [https://www.reuters.com/article/health-coronavirus-mexico-covax/mexico-makes-nearly-160-million-down-payment-for-covax-vaccine-plan-idUSKBN26W038 (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Iran]]
****[[Iran]] imposes additional restrictions for its capital [[Tehran]]. The new restrictions include making everyone wear a mask while indoors mandatory, and there is a fine of 500,000 [[Iranian rial|rials]] ($1.6) for violators who do not comply with the new rules. A partial shutdown implemented in the city last week is extended until October 16. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/10/10/iran-tightens-covid-19-rules-as-infections-continue-to-surge (Al Jazeera)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Nepal]]
****[[Nepal]] reports 5,008 new infections in the past 24 hours and taking the nationwide total at 105,684, the highest single day record of reported cases since the first cases were detected on January 23. [https://www.financialexpress.com/world-news/nepal-records-highest-single-day-spike-of-over-5000-new-covid-19-cases/2102637/lite/ (PTI via ''Financial Express'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil]]
***The number of COVID-19 deaths in [[Brazil]] exceeds 150,000. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-brazil-coronavirus/brazil-surpasses-150000-coronavirus-deaths-health-ministry-says-idUSKBN26V0YB (Reuters)]

;International relations
*[[North Korea and weapons of mass destruction]]
**[[North Korea]] holds a rare nighttime [[Military parades in North Korea|military parade]] featuring missiles to mark the [[Party Foundation Day|75th anniversary]] of the [[Workers' Party of Korea|Workers' Party]]. This was the country’s first military parade in two years. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-54491657 (BBC News)]

;Law and crime
*[[George Floyd protests]], [[2020–2021 United States racial unrest]]
**[[Shooting of Alvin Cole]]
***Authorities in [[Wauwatosa, Wisconsin|Wauwatosa]], [[Wisconsin]], announce that 28 people have been arrested during the third night of protests over the lack of charges against Joseph Mensah, the officer accused of killing 17-year-old Alvin Cole. [https://abcnews.go.com/amp/US/wireStory/28-arrests-wisconsin-protests-police-slaying-teen-73539404 (ABC News)]
***Demonstrations are held in [[Wauwatosa, Wisconsin|Wauwatosa]] for a fourth consecutive day following the [[Milwaukee County District Attorney]]'s decision not to prosecute Joseph Mensah for the fatal shooting of Alvin Cole. [https://www.jsonline.com/picture-gallery/news/2020/10/11/wauwatosa-police-officer-joseph-mensah-decision-alvin-cole-protests/5958595002/ (''Milwaukee Journal Sentinel'')]
**[[George Floyd protests in Kentucky]]
***Over 500 people march at [[Tyler Park, Louisville|Tyler Park]] in [[Louisville, Kentucky|Louisville]] to march in the name of [[Shooting of Breonna Taylor|Breonna Taylor]]. [[United States House of Representatives|Rep.]] [[John Yarmuth]], [[Kentucky House of Representatives|State Rep.]] [[Charles Booker (American politician)|Charles Booker]], [[Kentucky Senate|Kentucky State Senator]] [[Morgan McGarvey]], and Louisville Urban League President Sadiqa Reynolds speak at the Tyler Park protest. [https://www.courier-journal.com/story/news/local/breonna-taylor/2020/10/10/louisville-protests-white-protesters-march-honor-breonna-taylor/5910609002/ (''The Courier-Journal'')]
*[[Protests over responses to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Israel]], [[Corruption in Israel]]
***Protesters gather to call for the resignation of [[Prime Minister of Israel|Prime Minister]] [[Benjamin Netanyahu]] for allegations of [[Trial of Benjamin Netanyahu|corruption]] and his response to the COVID-19 pandemic in the [[Israel|country]]. [https://apnews.com/article/virus-outbreak-israel-jerusalem-trials-benjamin-netanyahu-fe7a32338f16b7fd3204f5c9b3c2fadd (AP)]
*[[Omnibus Law on Job Creation]], [[Indonesia omnibus law protests]]
**Authorities in [[Jakarta]] were cleaning up burned-out cars, government offices and bus shelters that were set ablaze by protesters enraged over an [[Omnibus Law on Job Creation|omnibus law]] they critics say will cripple labour rights and harm the environment. The authorities estimate the damage from the protest is Rp. 55 billion ([[United States dollar|US$]]3.7 million). [https://www.washingtonpost.com/business/jakarta-cleans-up-after-violent-anti-labor-law-protests/2020/10/09/cc90c6e0-0aa9-11eb-8719-0df159d14794_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[2020 Belarusian protests]]
**[[Alexander Lukashenko]], disputed [[President of Belarus]], visits opposition activists in a prison in [[Minsk]]. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/belarus-authoritarian-leader-visits-foes-prison-73539473 (ABC News)]

;Science and technology
*[[2020 in spaceflight]]
**Boulders are discovered on the [[101955 Bennu|Bennu]] asteroid by [[NASA]]'s [[OSIRIS-REx]] spacecraft, which is expected to collect samples from the [[asteroid]]'s surface later this month. [https://www.space.com/asteroid-bennu-formation-history-osiris-rex (Space.com)]
*[[NASA]] announces that the [[SpaceX Crew-1]] mission to the [[International Space Station]] would be delayed to mid-November. Furthermore, NASA calls for [[SpaceX]] satellite to investigate the issue that caused a [[GPS Block III]] to abort two seconds before launching on October 2. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/nasa-delays-next-crew-dragon-flight-in-wake-of-falcon-9-launch-abort-last-week/ (CBS News)]

;Sports
*[[2020 French Open]]
**[[Iga Świątek]] of [[Poland]] beats [[Sofia Kenin]] of the [[United States]] in the final of the [[2020 French Open - Women's Singles|Women's Singles]] 6–4, 6–1. Świątek became the first Polish tennis player to win a [[Grand Slam (tennis)|Grand Slam]] singles title. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/europe/polands-iga-swiatek-beats-sofia-kenin-for-french-open-title/2020/10/10/6a0fbb3e-0b08-11eb-8719-0df159d14794_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
